samb-p01-v01.speaker: Utpaladeva (maṅgala, praise voice)
samb-p01-v01.question: Under what auspice does the inquiry into relation open?
premises: With relation whose self is difference-and-non-difference (bhedābhedātmasaṃbandhasaha).
By whom all things are proved (sarvārthasādhitā); world-traffic (lokayātrā) is whose work (kṛtiḥ).
Him, Śiva, by own will (svecchayā), we praise (stumaḥ).
samb-p01-v01.inference: Auspice: the Lord whose will works world-traffic proves all things with difference-and-non-difference-relation.
uncertainties: Feminine adjectives (saha, sādhitā) lack an overt noun — implied śakti, or absolute construction; held open.
svecchayā's agency (his will grounding relation vs our will in praising) held open; read as his (svātantrya seed).

samb-p01-v02.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
samb-p01-v02.question: What is relation, at the opening thesis?
premises: Dawning (unmiṣan) by his body (vapuṣā) made of relation (mayena) through being, difference, and the rest (bhāvabhedādi).
Conquering (jayati) though one (ekaḥ api): world-self (viśvātmā), light (prakāśaḥ), supreme Lord (parameśvaraḥ).
samb-p01-v02.inference: Thesis stated: relation is the Lord's dawning body-form, not an accident of things.
uncertainties: kha reads bhedātma (whose self is difference) for bhedādi; main text followed, variant in NOTE.

samb-p01-v03.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
samb-p01-v03.question: Are awaiting or dependence the relation of inert things?
premises: Awaiting (apekṣā) and dependence (pāratantryam) are no relation (na saṃbandhaḥ) for the two inert (jaḍātmanoḥ).
From impossibility (asaṃbhavāt): even where selfhood is won (ātmalābhe'pi), it is metaphor (upacāraḥ), not definition (lakṣaṇā).

Prose (p.2-3): the sprout 'awaits' the seed only by courtesy; awaiting, longing-for-the-other's-disposal, checking one's own will are will-determinations (saṃkalpaviśeṣa) — and will is consciousness's.
samb-p01-v03.inference: First reduction fails: awaiting-language smuggles in the conscious relatum it should supply.

samb-p01-v04.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
samb-p01-v04.question: Is 'residing-in-two' the relation?
premises: From stating self-obtaining of non-beings (asatām ātmalābhokteḥ), two-seatedness (dviṣṭhatā) is likewise abandoned (hīyate).
Form-fusion alone (rūpasaṃśleṣa eva) thus stands (sthitaḥ) as relation's sense (saṃbandhārthaḥ).
Prose (p.2): duality and mutual separateness would be relations too; 'residing-in-two' is said of the pair, not the relation — state it plainly in its own form.
samb-p01-v04.inference: Second reduction fails: two-seatedness describes relata, never the relation; form-fusion stands in its place.

samb-p01-v05.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
samb-p01-v05.question: Is uninterruptedness the relation — and what positively is it?
premises: Not uninterruptedness (na ānantaryam): it misses relation (asaṃbandhāt) — else it would hold of iron bars (ayaḥśalākayoḥ).
Prose (p.2): distant father-son lack it, adjacent iron bars (even pervading substances) have it — neither necessary nor sufficient.
Hence (tena): fusion (śleṣaḥ) of the many's form — that alone is one-selfhood (aikātmyam eva).
samb-p01-v05.inference: Third reduction fails (with the iron-bars counterexample); positive thesis: relation is the many's form-fused one-selfhood.
uncertainties: asaṃbandhāt parsed as 'missing relation' (the mark fails to track); the grammar also allows 'from non-relation' — sense identical.

samb-p01-v06.speaker: Opponent (Dharmakīrtian; SP 5cd per MacCracken/Jha)
samb-p01-v06.question: Do the many need any unity at all?
premises: No barring (bādhaḥ) of the many even in one's unity (ekasyaikye'pi) — they say, as others do.
Things unmixed in themselves (amiśrāḥ svayaṃ bhāvāḥ) — thought (kalpanā) joins them (yojayati).
Witness: Dharmakīrti's Sambandhaparīkṣā v.5cd (Jha Philosophy of Relations; MacCracken) — the opponent's proof-text, quoted against him.
samb-p01-v06.inference: The Buddhist position in its own voice: unmixed things, thought-joined; unity needs no seat.

samb-p01-v07.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
samb-p01-v07.question: Is the joining only thought's fabrication?
premises: This (etat) is no mere thought (na kalpanāmātram): it cannot be warded off (avāraṇāt).
Like snake-error (sarpabhrānteḥ iva): its remedy fails (nivāraṇam) through clinging to a shining (ābhāsalagnatvāt).
Prose (p.5): even your side admits error clinging to thing-shining, unuprootable by refutation.
samb-p01-v07.inference: Retorsion begins: unwardability proves the joining is no mere fabrication.

samb-p01-v08.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
samb-p01-v08.question: What makes error stick?
premises: Clinging-to-shining (ābhāsalagnatvam) is not thing-resembling-shining (ābhāsasadṛśārthatā).
It is following-after-shining (ābhāsānusāritvaṃ): error is just that — an erred shining (bhrānta ābhāsa eva tat).
Prose (p.5): all errors concern resembling — but beyond resembling, errors hold by shining-clinging; else the silver-shell could not guide. Transaction-guiding seeming must follow the shining.
samb-p01-v08.inference: Error sticks by following shining, not resembling things: seeming that guides must trail being.

samb-p01-v09.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
samb-p01-v09.question: Can this justification be stated?
premises: Thus (ittham), in this very shining (asmin), such unity-seeing of the many (anekasyaikatādṛśi).
Its statable justification (vācyopapattiḥ) too is told (uktā), clearly (sphuṭam), in recognition's path (pratyabhijñānaye).
samb-p01-v09.inference: Warrant claimed: the many-seen-as-one is statable inside the Pratyabhijñā, plainly.

samb-p02-v10.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
samb-p02-v10.question: What of consciousness-bodied beings?
premises: Thus (evam), of beings (vastūnāṃ), of consciousness-bodied (cinmātravapuṣāṃ), of beings (satām).
Of Māyā-made-difference (māyānirmitabhedānām) even (api), unity (ekatvam) is not hard to effect (adurghaṭam).
samb-p02-v10.inference: Even Māyā-differenced beings take unity without strain — for the consciousness-bodied.

samb-p02-v11.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
samb-p02-v11.question: What is reflection's object for the worldly?
premises: Therein too (tatrāpi), what (yaḥ) is reflection's object (parāmarśaviṣayaḥ) for the worldly (laukikasya).
That (saḥ): of the knower (vedituḥ) whose pith (sāra) is difference (bheda) of non-difference-shining form (cidabhedaprathārūpa).
samb-p02-v11.inference: The worldly one's reflection-object is the knower whose pith is difference in non-difference-shining form.

samb-p02-v12.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
samb-p02-v12.question: Does blocked activity touch another thought?
premises: Activity (vyāpāraḥ) by this (anena) blocked (ruddhaḥ) — it (asau) should touch (spṛśet) no other thought (vikalpāntaram).
For on touching another thought (vikalpāntarasaṃsparśe) follows knower-difference (mātṛbhedaprasaṅgataḥ).
samb-p02-v12.inference: One reflection's business touches no other thought, or knowers multiply.

samb-p02-v13.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
samb-p02-v13.question: How do the many reach unity?
premises: Abiding in that-one-reflection (tadekāmarśavarti), by one-word-superimposition force (ekaśabdādhyāsavaśāt).
The many (anekaḥ) too would go (vrajet) to unity (ekatām) — as pot-cloth (ghaṭapaṭau) means (iti).
Prose: dvandva discussed at length — one reflection makes one word, one word one thing.
samb-p02-v13.inference: Many reach oneness through one-word superimposition — 'pot-cloth'.

samb-p02-v14.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
samb-p02-v14.question: Is there another relation?
premises: Thus (iti) there is (asti) also (tāvat?) another (anyaḥ): qualifier-qualified (viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyayoḥ) relation (saṃbandhaḥ).
For helping (upakārārthaḥ); it serves (upayujyate) for knowing (jñātum).
samb-p02-v14.inference: A second relation stands: qualifier-qualified, for helping, serving knowledge.

samb-p02-v15.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
samb-p02-v15.question: Is there twoness in manyness?
premises: Even in manyness (bahutve'pi), twoness (dvitvam) would be (bhavet).
From double-reflection birth (dvivimarśabhuvaḥ) — as the king's horses-chariots-men (rājño'śvarathapattayaḥ).
samb-p02-v15.inference: Manyness still yields twoness, double-reflection-born — like the king's retinue.
uncertainties: dvivimarśabhuvaḥ case read ablative (from); genitive ('of') equivalent in sense — settled.

samb-p02-v16.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
samb-p02-v16.question: How do the two reflections divide?
premises: Reflection (vimarśaḥ) 'of king' (rājñaḥ iti) is one (ekaḥ), facing own-generality (svasāmānyonmukhaḥ).
The other (paraḥ) — 'man' (puruṣaḥ iti), this (ayam), with master-generality-relation (svāmisāmānyasaṃbandhasahaḥ).
samb-p02-v16.inference: 'King' faces own-generality; 'man' faces the master's — two reflections, one relation.

samb-p02-v17.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
samb-p02-v17.question: How many thinkings?
premises: 'The king's man' (rājñaḥ puruṣaḥ iti) — this (eṣaḥ), after (paścāt), in relation's range (saṃbandhagocaraḥ).
Is to be thought (kalpyaḥ) by this (anena); or the former two to be thought (kalpyau) — those three (trayaḥ) in every way (sarvathā).
Prose: whole-thought after relation, or part-thoughts — three thinkings, all told.
samb-p02-v17.inference: Three thinkings: whole after relation, or the former two — all told.

samb-p02-v18.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
samb-p02-v18.question: Where does genitive-relation settle?
premises: Genitive-stated (ṣaṣṭhyādivācyaḥ) relation (saṃbandhaḥ), settled (viniviṣṭaḥ) in qualifier (viśeṣaṇe).
Reaching qualified-oneness (viśeṣyaikatvamāpanne), yet not abandoning (anujjhati) own form (svaṃ rūpam).
samb-p02-v18.inference: Genitive-relation settles in the qualifier, reaches oneness, keeps own form.

samb-p03-v19.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
samb-p03-v19.question: How do secondaries fit the chief?
premises: With one short (ekahānyā) — by the pure (śuddhena), by the chief (pradhānena) — mutual fitness (anyānyayogitā) would be (syāt) of the secondary (guṇasya).
As (yathā) the king's (rājñaḥ) man (puruṣaḥ), and (ca) the brahmin's.
Prose: chief/secondary pairs measured against king/man, brahmin/[kṣatriya?].
samb-p03-v19.inference: Secondaries fit the chief one-short of pure: king's man, brahmin's.
uncertainties: ekahānyā obscure (with-one-short? one short of what?) — held open as printed; no smoothing.

samb-p03-v20.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
samb-p03-v20.question: What other unity?
premises: So (tathā) by another (anyena) chief (pradhānena) — what (yā) other (anyā) unity (ekatā), or (vā) by still another (apareṇa).
Relation-called (saṃbandhākhyā) of the secondary (guṇasya) would be (syāt) — as (yathā) the king's horse (rājñaḥ aśvaḥ), man (puruṣaḥ).
samb-p03-v20.inference: Other chiefs, other unities: secondary's relation-called — king's horse, man.

samb-p03-v21.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
samb-p03-v21.question: What course is told?
premises: Thus (iti) relation's course (saṃbandhagatiḥ) told (uktā): resting-on-Māyā-knowers (māyīyajñātṛniṣṭhitāḥ)...
intellects (dhiyaḥ) of varied-thing-views (vibhinnārthadṛśaḥ), transaction-causing (vyavahārapravartikāḥ).
samb-p03-v21.inference: Course told: Māyā-knower-resting intellects drive transaction.

samb-p03-v22.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
samb-p03-v22.question: Are they deluded?
premises: Not (na) — but (paraṃ): those (tāḥ), so (tathā) erred (bhrāntāḥ) though called — all (sarvāḥ) even (api)...
moment by moment (pratikṣaṇāt) grounded (pratiṣṭhitāḥ) in endless-awareness (anantacit) reflection (vimarśa) called self-awareness (svasaṃvitsaṃjñaka).
samb-p03-v22.inference: Not deluded: moment-by-moment grounded in self-awareness-reflection.

samb-p03-v23.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
samb-p03-v23.question: What apparatus closes?
premises: Told (uktaḥ), self-awareness-proved (svasaṃvitsiddhaḥ), this (ayaṃ): unrefuted (nirbādhaḥ), useful (upayogavān)...

samb-p01-v01.plain_english: With relation whose self is difference-and-non-difference — by whom all things are proved, whose work is world-traffic — him, Śiva, by own will, we praise.
samb-p01-v01.sanskrit_cite: bhedābhedātmasaṃbandhasahasarvārthasādhitā lokayātrā kṛtiryasya svecchayā taṃ stumaḥ śivam

samb-p01-v02.plain_english: Dawning by a body made of relation through being, difference, and the rest — conquering though one: the world-self, light, the supreme Lord.
samb-p01-v02.sanskrit_cite: bhāvabhedādisaṃbandhamayena vapuṣonmiṣan jayatyeko'pi viśvātmā prakāśaḥ parameśvaraḥ

samb-p01-v03.plain_english: Awaiting and dependence are no relation for the two inert ones: impossible — even where selfhood is won, they are metaphor, not definition.
samb-p01-v03.sanskrit_cite: apekṣā pāratantryaṃ ca na saṃbandho jaḍātmanoḥ asaṃbhavādātmalābhe'pyupacāro na lakṣaṇā

samb-p01-v04.plain_english: From the teaching that non-beings obtain selfhood, two-seatedness too is abandoned: form-fusion alone thus stands as relation's meaning.
samb-p01-v04.sanskrit_cite: asatāmātmalābhokterdviṣṭhataivaṃ ca hīyate rūpasaṃśleṣa evaivaṃ saṃbandhārthaḥ sthitaḥ sa ca

samb-p01-v05.plain_english: Not uninterruptedness — for it misses relation: if it were so, it would hold of iron bars. Hence fusion of the many's form — that alone is one-selfhood.

samb-p01-v06.plain_english: No barring of the many in one's very oneness, others say: things unmixed in themselves — thought joins them.
samb-p01-v06.sanskrit_cite: naikasyaikye'pyanekasya bādha āhuryathā pare ityamiśrāḥ svayaṃ bhāvāstānyojayati kalpanā

samb-p01-v07.plain_english: Since this is no mere thought — it cannot be dismissed: like the snake-error, it resists remedy by clinging to a shining.

samb-p01-v08.plain_english: Since clinging to a shining is not a thing resembling a shining but a following after shining — error is exactly that: a shining astray.
samb-p01-v08.sanskrit_cite: yasmādābhāsalagnatvaṃ nābhāsasadṛśārthatā kiṃ tvābhāsānusāritvaṃ bhrānta ābhāsa eva tat

samb-p01-v09.plain_english: Thus even in this shining, the many's unity-seeing has a statable warrant — declared plainly in recognition's path.
samb-p01-v09.sanskrit_cite: itthamābhāsa evāsminnanekasyaikatādṛśi vācyopapattiḥ sāpyuktā pratyabhijñānaye sphuṭam

samb-p02-v10.plain_english: Thus, of beings, of consciousness-bodied beings — even of Māyā-difference-made, unity is not hard to effect.
samb-p02-v10.sanskrit_cite: evaṃ ca sati vastūnāṃ cinmātravapuṣāṃ satām māyānirmitabhedānāmapyekatvamadurghaṭam

samb-p02-v11.plain_english: Therein too, what is reflection's object for the worldly — that same: of the knower whose pith is difference of non-difference-shining form.
samb-p02-v11.sanskrit_cite: tatrāpi yaḥ parāmarśaviṣayo laukikasya saḥ cidabhedaprathārūpabhedasārasya vedituḥ

samb-p02-v12.plain_english: Activity blocked by this — it should touch no other thought; for on touching another thought, knower-difference follows.
samb-p02-v12.sanskrit_cite: vyāpāro'nena ruddho'sau na vikalpāntaraṃ spṛśet vikalpāntarasaṃsparśe mātṛbhedaprasaṅgataḥ

samb-p02-v13.plain_english: Abiding in that-one-reflection, by one-word-superimposition force — the many too would reach unity — as pot-cloth means.

samb-p02-v14.plain_english: So there is also another — qualifier-qualified relation, for helping; it serves for knowing.
samb-p02-v14.sanskrit_cite: ityasti tāvadanyaśca viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyayoḥ saṃbandha upakārārthaḥ sa jñātumupayujyate

samb-p02-v15.plain_english: Even in manyness there'd be twoness — from double-reflection birth — as the king's horses, chariots, men.

samb-p02-v16.plain_english: Reflection 'of king' is one, facing own-generality; the other — 'man,' this, with master-generality-relation.
samb-p02-v16.sanskrit_cite: vimarśo rājña ityekaḥ svasāmānyonmukhaḥ paraḥ svāmisāmānyasaṃbandhasahaḥ puruṣa ityayam

samb-p02-v17.plain_english: 'The king's man' — this, after, in relation's range — is to be thought by this; or the former two to be thought — those three in every way.
samb-p02-v17.sanskrit_cite: rājñaḥ puruṣa ityeṣa paścātsaṃbandhagocaraḥ kalpyo'nenātha vā kalpyau pūrvau te sarvathā trayaḥ

samb-p02-v18.plain_english: Genitive-stated relation, settled in the qualifier — reaching qualified-oneness, yet not abandoning own form.
samb-p02-v18.sanskrit_cite: ṣaṣṭhyādivācyaḥ saṃbandho viniviṣṭo viśeṣaṇe viśeṣyaikatvamāpanne svaṃ ca rūpamanujjhati

samb-p03-v19.plain_english: With one short — by the pure, by the chief — mutual fitness would be of the secondary — as the king's man, and the brahmin's.
samb-p03-v19.sanskrit_cite: ekahānyā pradhānena śuddhenānyānyayogitā syādguṇasya yathā rājñaḥ puruṣo brāhmaṇasya ca

samb-p03-v20.plain_english: So by another chief — what other unity, or by still another — relation-called of the secondary would be — as the king's horse, man.
samb-p03-v20.sanskrit_cite: tathānyena pradhānena yaikatānyāpareṇa vā saṃbandhākhyā guṇasya syādrājño'śvaḥ puruṣo

samb-p03-v21.plain_english: Thus relation's course told: resting-on-Māyā-knowers — intellects of varied-thing-views, transaction-causing.
samb-p03-v21.sanskrit_cite: iti saṃbandhagatyuktā māyīyajñātṛniṣṭhitāḥ dhiyo vibhinnārthadṛśo vyavahārapravartikāḥ

samb-p03-v22.plain_english: Not — but those, though called so erred — all even — moment by moment grounded in endless-awareness reflection called self-awareness.
samb-p03-v22.sanskrit_cite: na paraṃ tāstathā bhrāntāḥ sarvā api pratikṣaṇāt svasaṃvitsaṃjñakānantacidvimarśapratiṣṭhitāḥ

samb-p03-v23.plain_english: Told, self-awareness-proved, this: unrefuted, useful — relation in recognition — full apparatus besides.

essence: Relation's counterfeits are refused one by one — awaiting, two-seatedness, uninterruptedness need a consciousness they deny — until form-fusion stands: the many's one-selfhood (vv1-5).
The Buddhist proof-text is turned against its makers: unmixed things thought-joined is no mere thought but unwardable shining-clinging, warrantable in recognition's path (vv6-9).

sections.SUMMARY: Relation whose self is difference-and-non-difference proves all things; world-traffic is his work — Śiva, by own will, praised. His body dawns made of relation: conquering though one, world-self, light, supreme Lord. Awaiting and dependence are no relation for the two inert — impossible; won selfhood or not, metaphor, not definition. Teaching self-obtaining to non-beings drops two-seatedness: form-fusion alone stands as relation's sense. No unbroken nearness — it misses relation; else iron bars. So the many's form-fusion: one-selfhood alone. Others say the many need no barring in oneness: things unmixed, thought joins them. No mere thought, this — past warding, like snake-error clinging to a shining. Clinging is no thing-like-shining but trailing after it: error, that shining strayed. So many-seen-as-one finds warrant — statable, told clear in recognition's path.
sections.FUNCTION: Opens with praise and thesis, refuses three counterfeit relations, then turns the Buddhist proof-text through unwardability and shining-clinging to a warrant inside recognition.

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is exultation: three refusals, then the opponent's verse testifying against itself. The vyabhicāri is wonder that joining was never mere thought. Śāstric triumph-relish: truth winning by the adversary's own words.

essence: Unity without strain for the consciousness-bodied; the worldly one's reflection-object fixed as difference-pithed non-difference-shining (vv10-11).
Mechanics: one thought un-touched, one word uniting many, helping relation admitted, twoness in manyness, two facings, three thinkings, genitive settling unself-lost (vv12-18).

sections.SUMMARY: Even Māyā-differenced beings take unity without strain — the consciousness-bodied need no forcing. The worldly one's reflection-object is the knower whose pith is difference inside non-difference's shine. One reflection's business touches no other thought, or knowers multiply. The many still reach oneness through one-word superimposition — pot-cloth says it. A second relation stands, qualifier with qualified, for helping's sake: it serves to know. Even in many, twoness holds — double-grasp-begot, like the king's horses, chariots, men. Grasp 'of king' stands one, toward its own kind; 'man' the other, sharing the master-kind's bond. 'The king's man' — thought after, in relation's field, by this; or the first two thought — all three, always. Spoken by the sixth, relation settles in the qualifier — reaching oneness with the qualified, yet keeping its own shape.

sections.SUMMARY: One short of the pure chief, secondaries mutually fit — the king's man, and the brahmin's. By other chiefs, other unities — relation-called of secondaries: the king's horse, man. Not deluded, though called so — all, moment by moment, grounded in endless-awareness reflection called self-awareness. Told, self-awareness-proved, unrefuted, useful — relation in recognition: full apparatus besides.

lines: So, of beings, of consciousness-bodied beings —
even Māyā-differenced, unity comes not hard.

lines: There too, what the worldly reflect upon —
that same: the knower whose pith is difference of non-difference-shine.
samb-p02-v11.sanskrit_cite: tatrāpi yaḥ parāmarśaviṣayo laukikasya saḥ cidabhedaprathārūpabhedasārasya vedituḥ

lines: Its business, blocked by this —
let it touch no other thought: touching brings knower-split.

lines: Held in one reflection, by one word's laying-over —
the many still would reach oneness — 'pot-cloth'.
So there is also another — qualifier with qualified,
for helping's sake: it serves to know.
samb-p02-v14.sanskrit_cite: ityasti tāvadanyaśca viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyayoḥ saṃbandha upakārārthaḥ sa jñātumupayujyate

lines: Even in manyness, twoness would be —
born of double grasp — as the king's horses, chariots, men.
Grasp 'of king' stands one, facing its own kind —
'man' the other, sharing the master-kind's tie.
samb-p02-v16.sanskrit_cite: vimarśo rājña ityekaḥ svasāmānyonmukhaḥ paraḥ svāmisāmānyasaṃbandhasahaḥ puruṣa ityayam

lines: 'The king's man' — thought after, in relation's range,
thought by this; or the first two thought — all three, always.
samb-p02-v17.sanskrit_cite: rājñaḥ puruṣa ityeṣa paścātsaṃbandhagocaraḥ kalpyo'nenātha vā kalpyau pūrvau te sarvathā trayaḥ

lines: Genitive-spoken, relation settles in the qualifier —
reaching oneness with the qualified, yet keeping its own shape.
samb-p02-v18.sanskrit_cite: ṣaṣṭhyādivācyaḥ saṃbandho viniviṣṭo viśeṣaṇe viśeṣyaikatvamāpanne svaṃ ca rūpamanujjhati

lines: One short — yet by the chief, by the pure — secondaries fit each other —
the king's man, and the brahmin's.
samb-p03-v19.sanskrit_cite: ekahānyā pradhānena śuddhenānyānyayogitā syādguṇasya yathā rājñaḥ puruṣo brāhmaṇasya ca
notes: ekahānyā held open (one short of what?)

lines: So by another chief — what other unity, or by still another —
secondaries called relation: the king's horse, man.
samb-p03-v20.sanskrit_cite: tathānyena pradhānena yaikatānyāpareṇa vā saṃbandhākhyā guṇasya syādrājño'śvaḥ puruṣo

lines: So relation's course is told: intellects
resting on Māyā-knowers, of varied views, driving transaction.
samb-p03-v21.sanskrit_cite: iti saṃbandhagatyuktā māyīyajñātṛniṣṭhitāḥ dhiyo vibhinnārthadṛśo vyavahārapravartikāḥ

lines: Not deluded — though called erring, all of them,
moment by moment, grounded in endless-awareness reflection.

relation in recognition — full apparatus besides.
